sentences.text: All lower jaws found are remarkably straight.
While initially estimated at 4.26 meters, the wingspan is now thought to be no more than 2 meters.
A fossil site near Yacimiento de Fuente Amarga was discovered in 1980.
Ten fossiliferous blocks containing pterosaur bones were recovered in 1993 and 1994.
The genus name Prejanopterus is derived from the village of Préjano and the Greek word for wing.
The species name curvirostra refers to a claimed distinctive leftward bend in the snout.
Later studies indicate the snout has a slight dorsal curvature rather than a sideways bend.
The specific name was emended to curvirostris because the original feminine form was incorrect.
The holotype specimen F. A. 112 consists of a fragmented snout.
Specimen F. A. 185, another snout, serves as the paratype.
A 2012 study positioned Prejanopterus as a pterodactylid between the genus Pterodactylus and the group Ctenochasmatoidea.
Prejanopterus lived during the Lower Cretaceous (lower Aptian age) in the Lezas Formation of La Rioja, Spain.
Prejanopterus lived between 121.4 and 119.57 million years ago.
Some researchers suggest Prejanopterus might be a lonchodectid based on its unusual tooth socket morphology and jaw shape.
